sample_unit: interview participants (nursing interns, preceptors, head nurses, administrators, IT specialists, quality officer)

links.outcome: Informal, unsanctioned generative AI use by nursing interns on personal devices amid lack of governance
links.effect: Interns used generative AI on personal devices during clinical placement while institutional governance had not kept pace; participants across all stakeholder groups called for tiered governance.
links.quote: Interns use it on personal devices, yet institutional governance has not kept pace.

links.outcome: Presence of institutional AI rules governing intern use during placement
links.effect: Theme 1 identified multilevel discretionary rule-making in a policy vacuum, with a cross-stakeholder call for institutional frameworks.
links.quote: Five interconnected themes emerged: (1) multilevel discretionary rule-making in a policy vacuum; (2) a universally endorsed but unevenly enacted verification imperative; (3) intuitive risk stratification; (4) tensions between standardised AI outputs and embodied nursing care; and (5) a cross-stakeholder call for institutional frameworks.

links.outcome: Whether staff verify AI outputs before acting on them
links.effect: Verification was universally endorsed by stakeholders but unevenly enacted in practice (qualitative theme; no numbers reported).
links.quote: Five interconnected themes emerged: (1) multilevel discretionary rule-making in a policy vacuum; (2) a universally endorsed but unevenly enacted verification imperative; (3) intuitive risk stratification; (4) tensions between standardised AI outputs and embodied nursing care; and (5) a cross-stakeholder call for institutional frameworks.

unlisted_practices: AI literacy training for nursing students integrated into curricula
Preceptor development for supervising AI use in clinical placement

screen.reason: Qualitative study examining the informal use and governance of generative AI by nursing interns and supervisors during real clinical placements.
